text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 45

An all-male panel in economics is unremarkable on its own — the field is roughly 25–30% women, so four men is close to chance. Alone, it proves nothing and makes a weak opening argument.

Your real case is the credential gap: completed PhD vs. unfinished, six papers vs. two, four years teaching vs. unquantified "industry experience." Ask whether the advertised criteria actually required a completed doctorate, and how "industry experience" was weighted and scored.

Lead with that, plus the unanswered request — a public university usually owes written reasons within a set period, and silence is a procedural failing you can escalate.

Mention panel composition as context, not as your central claim.
